To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of imperfect carrier phase recovery on the mean SNRs of coherent and differentials coherent PSK systems is negligible.
the effect of imperfect carrier recovery on the performance of equal-gain combining (EGC) is significant, and that the performance of EGC can be improved through signal combination.
carrier phase errors cause an increase in the mean bit error rate of a coherent EGC system and that the carrier phase errors can be reduced through diversity combining.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance analysis of EGC with Tikhonov phase references and partially coherent Rayleigh fading signals.
the analysis of EGC with partially coherent fading signal, the computation of the effect of phase errors on the error probability, and the computation of the phase precision requirement.
the effect of carrier-phase errors on the error performance of diversity combiners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the carrier phase errors are not a major concern for coherent detection, and that the carrier recovery loops can be designed for a low SNR reliability level, and that the signal combination can be used to further reduce the carrier phase precision requirements.
EGC is a viable option for coherent and noncoherent detection of partially coherent signals, provided that the carrier phase errors are small.
carrier phase errors are a serious limitation on the performance of a diversity combiner, and that this limitation can be reduced by using differentially coherent detection and signal combination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carrier phase error effect on the mean SNRs is negligible but it is significant for small bit error probability or deep fades.
the carrier phase errors can be reduced through diversity combining.
the effect of the carrier phase errors on error-rate performance can be significantly reduced through diversity and signal combination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carrier phase error can be tolerated in the presence of diversity.
a coherent EGC receiver with imperfect phase synchronization can be used to improve the performance of a differentially coherent receiver.
the carrier phase errors can be tolerated by EGC if their variance is small compared to the variance of the fading envelope.
